commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Mai and Zuko ({1}{U}{B}{R}) turn both artifacts and Allies into instant-speed spells while firebending3 turns their combat into red-mana casting windows. Flash artifact/Ally value and attack-driven combustion with disciplined compact artifact wins, not independent generic turbo.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Bracket 4 — Optimized. High-powered artifact combo/value deck with unique combat-mana flash windows; limited to 31 flexible lands and Grixis pip requirements, not proven top-table cEDH.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Reject Thassa's Oracle plus Demonic Consultation/Tainted Pact transformation; preserve ten Ally creatures, combat firebending and flash artifact utility as genuine distinct pillars.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: Whole 99 assessed by attack/flash payoffs, ten Ally creatures, thirty-three artifact spells, color ramp and 31 mana/land faces, compact 3 combo families, card advantage, artifact activated costs, stack interaction, graveyard hate, spot removal, sorcery and combo vulnerabilities. Individual expensive Avatar Roku and Tundra Tank contrasted with commander-specific Fire Nation Turret and Forensic Gadgeteer; all high-power staple slots challenged without homogenization.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: 31 physical land faces including Soporific Springs MDFC. The three land replacements remove unconditional taplands Xander's Lounge and Path of Ancestry, then add Verdant fetch in place of a BR painland. The source's 20k finite simplified test for the common five-swap package raised T4 commander deployment proxy 52.53% to 54.49%, while its six-swap Grim package reached only 52.42%; extra engine swaps have NOT been win-rate simulated.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Kept counters Fierce Guardianship, Force of Will, Mana Drain, Swan Song, Offer, Deflecting Swat, Deadly Rollick, and Cyclonic Rift, with new Pact; Sink is versatile but temporary. Jeska replaces Chaos Warp, losing true permanent/stack-independent answer. Tundra Tank and Greaves protection leave for Forensic and Pact, lowering proactive commander resilience. Bojuka Bog and Boiling Rock Rioter remain grave hate.

weakest_slots.weakness: Six-mana triple-red off-type creature cannot use Mai and Zuko's artifact or Ally flash and appears late in a 31-land deck.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Three-mana artifact arrives at flash and gives commander an additional firebending2 in future combats; accepts loss of six red on every player's attacks.

weakest_slots.weakness: Three-mana Vehicle needs crew to attack for its firebending1; most timely value is a one-turn indestructible ETB.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Gadgeteer creates Clues during instant-speed artifact chains and converts Basalt into an independent infinite-mana engine, while acknowledging protection loss.

weakest_slots.weakness: Always enters tapped and only scries on matching Human/Noble/Ally casts while the plan prioritizes early four-mana deployment.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Thirty-three artifact spells plus cheap permanents enable dependable colored production now rather than on following turn.

weakest_slots.weakness: Unconditional tapped triome materially suppresses flash-window deployment in low 31-land source.
weakest_slots.reasoning: An optional untapped blue mana MDFC with bounce-spell floor improves tempo and instant interaction; sacrifices tricolor typing.

weakest_slots.weakness: BR painland cannot supply U for a four-color-symbol split requirement and no graveyard fetch synergy.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Fetches the necessary color pair from existing Grixis typed duals, trading search reliance and life for flexibility.

weakest_slots.weakness: Single three-mana catch-all, useful but does not increase proactive deployment or artifact storm turns.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Main-phase red mana and impulse selection accelerate artifact storm; enchantment-answer loss expressly recorded as material.

weakest_slots.weakness: Shroud prevents some own targeted protection, and Greaves itself does not counter stack interaction; does grant important haste.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Zero-cost protection on an actual win turn replaces proactive haste/protection; upkeep 3UU is a serious risk.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: October 14 100/100 locked predecessor already carries Basalt/Rings, Citadel/Top/Reservoir, Breach/LED/Freeze, flashable artifact creatures, ten Allies, instant-speed untapping, premium blue counters and draw. These are not casually removed.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: Reviewed current Scryfall and 2026-10-23 EDHREC general/upgraded/optimized/cEDH inclusion and High Lift, 208 nearly-included Commander Spellbook interactions, source-bound 20k finite goldfish and 96-cell Pact grid, plus selected independent WotC Oracle/Forensic and off-ranking artifact utilities.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: Forensic Gadgeteer's cost reduction and Basalt loop is stronger than overlooked protection Vehicle Tundra Tank; Fire Nation Turret is a reliable commander-centered combat amplifier at a more accessible slot than six-mana Roku. Eight+ wider packages all demand sacrifice of interaction, grave hate, colored fixing, protected artifact tools or Ally depth.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Three land quality moves improve the commander turn; Jeska plus Pact consolidate explosive setup/stack protection while conceding Chaos Warp and Greaves; Turret plus Gadgeteer lower the curve and create two distinct commander-led artifact/combat engine gains versus slow high-red Roku and narrow one-shot vehicle. Seven full swaps are a strategic decision, not a five-swap floor.

final_candidate.deckwide_reconciliation: 100 physical cards, 100 distinct exact names, one Mai and Zuko Commander, no companion, 31 physical land faces including one MDFC, 33 artifact spells and 10 Allies including commander. All 99 source-snapshot names plus one independently sourced Forensic Gadgeteer fall in UBR and currently officially Commander legal. Seven exact additions and seven cuts reconciled with frozen aa2036f4 predecessor; no project exceptions.

owner_authority.owner_approval_question: This deck is complete. Do you approve it?

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: All remaining slots post five-swap draft were reconsidered by role. Two additional commander-relevant weak spots were found at 6-mana triple-red nonflash Roku and the limited one-shot Tank Vehicle; Forensic Gadgeteer and Fire Nation Turret improve multiple engine dimensions rather than serving as filler. A third increase to eight would require losing Bog graveyard hate, colored talisman rock, essential Deluge or Ally count, so seven is defended by effects.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Reject eighth, since small untapped mana consistency does not represent enemy graveyard risk in source proxy and loses the clean mass graveyard exile.
Reject extra ninth because prelegend dead zero-mana accelerator sacrifices crucial reliable Grixis colored access.

open_ended_optimization_audit.no_credible_larger_package_reason: The tested alternatives for an eighth would remove the remaining primary graveyard hate, a two-mana colored rock, the unique general board wipe, or another high-leverage Ally/artifact engine; none yields robust improvement across the full commander's states.
open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: Stopped at seven genuine one-for-one changes on effect comparisons, not because seven is a project ceiling. Following the five WIP improvements, Turret and Forensic were extra independent commander-first wins; further alternatives introduce a disproportionate loss of graveyard interruption, blue/black/red fixing, board control, or flash-available Ally/artifact card draw. No stronger eighth card survives the adversarial challenger tradeoff based on these sources and bounded tests.
